summary: This case study details a split-store architecture separating user identity (Cloudflare D1) from marketplace state (PostgreSQL) while utilizing short-lived, path-bound HMAC assertions to secure communication between the Edge worker and Node control plane. The article provides precise code implementations, security boundaries, and defense mechanisms against relative path traversal vulnerabilities.
strengths: Clear and practical architectural separation of website identity and marketplace state
Detailed code snippets demonstrating HMAC-SHA256 assertion generation and verification
Specific handling of WHATWG URL parsing edge cases to prevent host spoofing via double-slash paths
Well-defined security boundary ensuring unmixed credentials across browser, worker, and control plane
weaknesses: Relies on code snippets from a private repository without a public runnable reproduction artifact
Omits server-side nonce (jti) tracking, relying solely on short-lived expiration and path binding
suggestions: Provide a public minimal repository containing the exact worker and verifier test suite for reproducibility
Expand on the tradeoffs regarding the absence of server-side jti nonce tracking

claims.text: Cloudflare D1 stores users, password hashes, verification and reset token hashes, and browser sessions.
Web Crypto HMAC-SHA256 is used for generating the request assertions.
Passing a request-controlled path into new URL(userPath, origin) treats a string beginning with // as a scheme-relative URL.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Mac host pairing with four unmixed credentials and a loopback Network.framework panel
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on edge-to-control-plane website session bridging via short-lived HMAC assertions rather than Mac host pairing.
